problem.claim: Whether strong language-model capabilities can be achieved with diffusion models rather than autoregressive models.

gap.claim: The abstract identifies a common assumption that core LLM capabilities inherently depend on autoregressive models.

contributions.claim: Introduces LLaDA, a diffusion language model trained from scratch with pre-training and supervised fine-tuning.
Uses forward data masking and Transformer-parameterized reverse generation to predict masked tokens, with likelihood-lower-bound optimization for probabilistic inference.

Reports scalable performance comparable to self-constructed autoregressive baselines and competitiveness with selected strong LLMs on in-context learning, instruction following, and reversal-curse evaluation.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors present LLaDA as a diffusion-based alternative that challenges the assumed necessity of autoregressive models for core LLM capabilities.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Across benchmarks covering general tasks, math, and code, the authors report strong scalability and performance comparable to their self-constructed autoregressive baselines.
The authors report that LLaDA 8B is competitive with LLaMA3 8B for in-context learning and, after supervised fine-tuning, shows impressive instruction following in multi-turn dialogue case studies.
The authors report that LLaDA surpasses GPT-4o on a reversal poem completion task related to the reversal curse.

narrative_sequence.summary: The paper starts from the widespread view that LLM capabilities rely on autoregressive models.
It introduces LLaDA, trained from scratch under pre-training and supervised fine-tuning.
LLaDA combines forward masking with reverse masked-token generation through a Transformer and likelihood-lower-bound training.
Reported benchmark and case-study results show scalability and selected task competitiveness, motivating a challenge to autoregressive necessity.

source_observation.claim: The abstract links a specific masking/reverse-generation mechanism to a broad capability claim, then reports comparisons across general, math, code, in-context learning, instruction following, and reversal-curse tasks.

lessons.interpretation: A compact abstract can make an architectural challenge legible by pairing mechanism, evaluation scope, and a clearly stated implication.
lessons.application: When proposing a nonstandard architecture, state its core training/generation operation before grouping evidence by capability and comparison target.
lessons.exception: This framing is unsuitable when the work has no concrete mechanism or when evaluation scope is too narrow to support a broad architectural implication.

unknowns: The abstract gives no benchmark sizes, numerical scores, statistical analyses, or detailed scaling setup.
Details of the reversal poem completion task and the GPT-4o comparison protocol are unspecified.
The abstract does not establish priority, independently verified validity, or reproducibility beyond mentioning project code.
